quarterly_data.signal: Fenebrutinib Phase III data at MSToronto2026 (late-breaking): versus active comparators, fenebrutinib reduced slowly expanding lesion volume by up to 30% (p<0.001) in RMS (96 weeks) and PPMS (120 weeks) and accumulation of paramagnetic rim lesions by 62% (p=0.001) in RMS. Pooled FENhance 1 and 2 (RMS): annualised relapse rate reduced 55% versus comparator (p<0.001) over 96 weeks, annual total brain volume loss reduced 23% (p<0.001), 12-week composite confirmed disability progression reduced 16% (p=0.04), and 75% of patients showed no evidence of disease activity (NEDA-3) at nearly two years, a 70% reduction (p<0.001) versus comparator. Roche says the data support fenebrutinib's potential as the first and only high-efficacy oral medicine for both relapsing and primary progressive MS.

quarterly_data.signal: Ocrevus: the European Commission approved Ocrevus for paediatric relapsing MS (children 10 years and older) on 15 October, following FDA approval in May. New Phase III OPERETTA 2 data: 90% of children aged 10-17 at trial entry remained relapse-free over two years, and pre-existing immunity to common childhood vaccines was preserved in 81-100% of patients; Phase IIIb CONSONANCE: 53% of participants over 55 showed no disability progression after two years, similar to younger participants (55%).

quarterly_data.signal: Enspryng in MOGAD (exploratory analyses of the pivotal Phase III METEOROID trial): patients achieved numerically superior recovery 12 weeks after a relapse versus placebo (median EDSS change -2 vs -0.5), with overall function stable (median 0) versus worsening (median 0.5) on placebo; Roche says this reinforces Enspryng's potential to become the first FDA-approved treatment for MOGAD.
